text:
mike: heads up — saw ~12% tail latency regression on TP all-reduce after the canary. small message sizes (~1–4KB) blow up when KV cache warms/evicts.
anya: ugh. which model/shape and can you attach the microprofile?
mike: running microbench on 8-GPU TP (s0..s7), model shape 2048x1. quick nsys excerpt below: 
```
GPU activities:  comm [NCCL]  p95=18.2ms p99=46.9ms
Host: kernel scheduling stalls around kv.flush calls
Trace: bursts of many tiny allreduce ops (~2.4K each) instead of batched chunks
```
mike: command I used: `./tp_allreduce_bench --msgsize 2k --iters 2000 --profile nsys`
infra-bot: deploy-canary #2240 rolled at 2026-03-17T18:12Z :package:
elda: does the runtime currently pick kernel based on token_count only? if so, frag/byte-size effects might be causing lots of tiny NCCL launches.
ken: can we repro with forced tree algorithm? my gut: ring overhead for many small messages + non-coalesced sends = high latency. try forcing NCCL_ALGO=tree and increasing coalesce threshold to 8KB.
anya: please paste a short before/after numbers when you test. even p95/p99 is enough.
mike: quick numbers from local repro (8 GPUs):
- baseline (ring, default coalesce): p95=42ms p99=98ms
- tree forced: p95=30ms p99=52ms
- ring + coalesce_threshold=8KB: p95=33ms p99=45ms
ken: nice — both tree and coalescing help. suggests problem is fragmentation creating many tiny allreduces. also saw kernel_picker flipping between fp16/int8 kernels in logs which adds jitter.
elda: two actionable items: 1) make kernel selection stable across small-msg steady-state (avoid oscillation), 2) bump default coalesce threshold for TP pipelines where kv.flush frequency is high.
anya: also check KV cache eviction pattern — if flush occurs mid-step we get chop() that yields small msg sizes. add trace around `kv.flush()` and runtime packer to confirm.
ken: I'll gate a canary that enables tree for msgsize<=8KB and raises coalesce to 8KB for TP routes only. will run scaled microbench (64 iter buckets) and post metrics.
infra-bot: linked PR and run: <https://github.com/redwood-inc/repo/pull/1234|PR#1234> CI: perf-bench queued.
mike: filed regression label + minimal repro and attached `nsys` trace. PR reference in thread. thanks all — prioritizing this for next deploy window. :thumbsup:
